method: All 15 openings, all 39 five-ply reply disagreements and 12 evenly spaced agreeing reply controls. Opening contenders are the top two five-ply moves plus every move within .040 at any of three/four/five plies and the XG leader. Every retained five-ply reply contender is included. Fixed trials per candidate/policy; no significance-driven early stopping. Independent 32-trial batches, common seeds across candidates and policies. Money Jacoby, no beavers. Fixed accuracy comparison: Basic versus Short/deep; full-game Balanced and Strong have implementation checks only.

limitations: The cohort deliberately includes five-ply disagreements; it is not a random sample of all backgammon positions.
XG historical rollouts and XGRoller++ are approximate references; some gaps are below their reported uncertainty.
The XG source enables beavers, while these GNUbg rollouts do not. Earlier three-ply context checks found negligible effects, but rollout equivalence is untested.
Sampling intervals exclude policy/model bias and candidate-screening risk. Leader-gap intervals are unadjusted exploratory comparisons, not simultaneous guarantees.

Basic simulates complete games; Short/deep truncates after five turns using GNUbg two-ply endpoint evaluation. This reduces sampling noise but retains endpoint-model bias. All policies use normal move filters and may accept a clear shallow winner.

planAmendment.reason: Narrowed to the original Basic baseline versus the completed Short/deep policy. Full-game Balanced adds substantial simulation cost; it and full-game Strong retain implementation checks only. No candidate, seed, or trial is dropped for either published policy. Decision made before corrected-run Balanced results were available.
